resolutions.finding: G2: tour_captures.py is broken at the pinned commit and nobody says so.
resolutions.truth: See C4 above; settled against both project.yml:52-56 and project.pbxproj:308-331. ADDITIONAL DEFECT the critic did not find, in the same function: scripts/tour_captures.py:109-129 `capture()` has NO launch wait. It starts `deadline = time.time() + 630` at :118 immediately after `open -n` at :117, then at :119-123 does `time.sleep(2)` and breaks out of the loop the first time `pgrep -f <marker>` finds nothing. Because a fresh bundle can take far longer than 2 s to appear through LaunchServices, the loop can break before the run has even started and `encode()` then exits with 'The capture run wrote no <source>.png' (:260). scripts/website_captures.py:133-151 `wait_for_run` is the fixed version of the same loop and says so at :136-137 ('The app takes a moment to appear through LaunchServices, so the run is first waited into existence'), waiting up to 60 x 2 s for the process to appear BEFORE starting the budget. tour_captures.py never got that fix. Note also the pgrep invocations differ: tour_captures.py:121/:125 use `pgrep -f <marker>` / `pkill -9 -f <marker>` with marker `"tour-captures " + str(CAPTURES)` (no leading dashes, no `--` separator); website_captures.py:140/:147/:150 use `pgrep -f -- <marker>` / `pkill -9 -f -- <marker>` with markers `"website-captures " + str(CAPTURES)` (:121) and `"--tour-captures " + str(TOUR_CAPTURES)` (:162).

Record both tour_captures.py defects so no one 'ports the bug' by copying :36 and :109-129 verbatim.

resolutions.finding: G3: capture budget mismatch. TourCaptures watchdog 600 s; tour_captures.py waits 630 s; website_captures.py waits 330 s for the same run and then pkill -9.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, all four literals verified. DroppyCode/App/Captures/TourCaptures.swift:51-56: comment '// Thirty-odd stills, each with an activation wait: ten minutes of budget.' then `Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(600)); WebsiteCaptures.log("out of time, quitting"); exit(0) }`. DroppyCode/App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift:306-312: `Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(110)); log("out of time, quitting"); exit(0) }`. scripts/tour_captures.py:118 `deadline = time.time() + 630` (above 600, correct). scripts/website_captures.py:163-164 launches `--tour-captures` then `wait_for_run(marker, 330)`, and wait_for_run:150 ends with `subprocess.run(["pkill", "-9", "-f", "--", marker])` and prints 'the run overran its budget and was killed'. 330 s is 270 s BELOW the app's own 600 s deadline, so the default `scripts/website_captures.py` invocation kills a healthy tour run less than 6 minutes in. The run has to photograph at least 26 web-theme stills (TourCaptures.swift:201-209, one per AppTheme case, each with a 650 ms settle at :206 plus an activation wait) on top of roughly 20 other stills, which is exactly why the app's own author budgeted ten minutes. The `--website-captures` pairing is safer than the critic implies: website_captures.py:123 `wait_for_run(marker, 120)` against the in-app 110 s, and wait_for_run's launch-detection loop (:138-143, up to 60 x 2 s) runs BEFORE the budget starts, so the effective allowance is 120 s measured from the moment the process is first seen, against a 110 s in-app watchdog measured from `run()` entry.
resolutions.port_impact: UPSTREAM DEFECT to record, not to copy. If the port keeps capture tooling, the external budget must exceed the in-process watchdog, and the two numbers must come from one place. The literals to carry forward if the subsystem is ported: in-process tour watchdog 600 s, in-process website watchdog 110 s, both ending in an immediate `exit(0)` after a log line.

resolutions.finding: G7: R056 misreads WINDOW_SIZES as authoritative; the per-still JSON sidecar is authoritative and WINDOW_SIZES is only the legacy fallback. The 'web-* names missing from WINDOW_SIZES' question is moot.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. scripts/tour_captures.py:161-183 `interior(name, inset=8)` opens `<name>.png`, and at :173-178 uses `<name>.json` when it exists, reading `frames["rect"]` (taking rect_w, rect_h) and `frames["window"]` (x, y, w, h) with `scale = image.width / rect_w`. Only at :179-181, when the sidecar is absent, does it fall back to `window_box(name)` with `scale = 2`, and the docstring at :169-170 says the table 'is exact only for window-only stills'. scripts/tour_captures.py:215-236 `frame(name, inset=8)` returns `interior(name, inset)` outright when the sidecar is missing (:220-221) and otherwise cuts from `frames["rect"]`/`frames["window"]`/`frames.get("focus")` via `focus_box` (:186-212), with a second pass at :230-234 when a focus is taller than the window. The sidecar is written on EVERY successful still: DroppyCode/App/Captures/WebsiteCaptures.swift:948-963 `still(_:_:focus:)` calls `writeSidecar(for:rect:focus:)` at :959 unconditionally after writing the PNG, and writeSidecar (:974-985) emits keys exactly `rect` = [rect.minX, rect.minY, rect.width, rect.height] and `window` = [window.minX - rect.minX, rect.maxY - window.maxY, window.width, window.height], plus `focus` (same transform) only when a focus was given, serialized with JSONSerialization `.sortedKeys`. Its only early return is `guard let window = stage?.windowFrame` (:975), and Stage.windowFrame (:670) is `window?.frame`, which survives `setWindowHidden(true)` (:718-726 uses orderOut, it does not release the window). CONSUMPTION: tour_captures.py:252-262 `encode()` passes exactly SEVEN names through `frame()` - tour-welcome, tour-hydra, tour-pairs, tour-slider, tour-threads, tour-recipes, tour-panels - then writes tour-themes from `theme_mosaic()` (:239-249), which calls `interior()` on the four `tour-theme-<id>` stills for THEME_ORDER = ["tokyoNight", "gruvbox", "catppuccinLatte", "rosePine"] (:76). No `web-*` name ever reaches `frame()` or `interior()` in this script; every web-* still is encoded by website_captures.py `tour_still()` (:176-183), which never opens a sidecar and only caps width. For the record, WINDOW_SIZES (tour_captures.py:53-75) has exactly 23 entries: tour-welcome, web-hero, tour-hydra, tour-pairs, tour-slider, tour-threads, tour-recipes, tour-panels, tour-window, web-diff, web-palette, web-plans, web-question, web-queue, web-intro, tour-theme-tokyoNight, tour-theme-gruvbox, tour-theme-catppuccinLatte, tour-theme-rosePine, web-theme-tokyoNight, web-theme-gruvbox, web-theme-catppuccinLatte, web-theme-rosePine. TOUR_STILLS (website_captures.py:49-69) has exactly 18 entries, so web-slash, web-quote and web-notify are indeed in TOUR_STILLS and absent from WINDOW_SIZES, and it does not matter.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT: the geometry contract between the app and the encoder is the per-still JSON sidecar with keys `rect`, `window` and optional `focus`, all in points with a top-left origin, and the pixel scale is derived as PNG width / rect width, never assumed to be 2. A Windows port that reimplements capture must write the same three keys with the same transform. WINDOW_SIZES is legacy and must not be treated as the spec.

The twelve the critic lists are all verbatim-correct and correctly line-numbered. ON THE ICON PRECONDITION the critic is right: package_dmg.sh:46 `VOLUME_ICON_SOURCE="$APP_PATH/Contents/Resources/AppIcon.icns"` and :47 refuses without it; :76 `cp "$VOLUME_ICON_SOURCE" "$STAGE_PATH/.VolumeIcon.icns"`. The icon source in the repository is the Icon Composer bundle DroppyCode/Resources/AppIcon.icon (contents: icon.json plus Assets/{SVG Image.svg, mascot (3).png, mascot dark.png, shadow dark.png, shadow def.png}), selected by `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIcon` (project.yml:47; pbxproj:286 and :311). SOURCE FACT: the DMG step depends on the app bundle already carrying a compiled AppIcon.icns. ENGINEERING inference (not provable from the checkout): that the .icon compilation is what emits Contents/Resources/AppIcon.icns.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT: the packaging step has 16 distinct failure messages, all on stderr with the `package_dmg: ` prefix and exit code 1. A Windows installer script that claims parity on diagnostics needs all 16 conditions, not 12. The load-bearing ordering fact for the port: icon compilation must precede installer packaging, because the installer's volume icon is copied OUT of the built bundle, not out of the repository. Other exact literals: VOLNAME 'Droppy Code' (:25), APP_BUNDLE_NAME '$VOLNAME.app' (:26), background asset release/dmg/installer-background.tiff (:17), DS_Store asset release/dmg/installer-DS_Store.base64 stored base64-encoded so git treats it as source (:18-19), work dir template `/tmp/droppy-code-dmg-XXXX` (:49), intermediate format UDRW with fs HFS+ (:78), final format ULMO (:113), FinderInfo xattr written as the exact 32-byte hex string with kHasCustomIcon 0x0400 at byte offset 8 (:92-94), and 8 polite detach attempts one second apart before the forced detach (:97-106).

resolutions.finding: G9: sync_dev_data.sh mirrors only four API-key accounts while rsyncing mcp.json; MCP secrets live in the same Keychain service under different accounts, so a mirror copies MCP configuration without its secrets, contradicting quick_run.sh's header.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, and it is a real defect. DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift:7-9 `private static func account(server: String, field: String) -> String { "MCP " + server + " " + field }`, and :15 / :39 use `kSecAttrService as String: AppInfo.name`, the SAME service as every API key (DroppyCode/Services/Providers/APIKeychain.swift:31, :61 also `AppInfo.name`). AppInfo.name is `Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleDisplayName") as? String ?? "Droppy Code"` (DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:4), so 'Droppy Code' in Release and 'Droppy Code Dev' in Debug. scripts/sync_dev_data.sh:36 `rsync -a --delete "$RELEASE_LIB/" "$DEV_LIB/"` mirrors the whole ~/Library/Application Support/<name> library, which is Storage.root, and mcp.json lives there: DroppyCode/Core/Models/MCP.swift:244 `static let connectionsURL = Storage.root.appendingPathComponent("mcp.json")` and :246 `customsURL = Storage.root.appendingPathComponent("custom-mcp.json")`, with MCP.swift:186 stating the state is 'kept in `Storage.root/mcp.json`. Secrets live in' the Keychain. sync_dev_data.sh:40-45 then `defaults delete "$DEV_DOMAIN"` and `defaults export "$RELEASE_DOMAIN" - | defaults import "$DEV_DOMAIN" -`. But sync_dev_data.sh:49 iterates exactly four accounts: `for account in "DeepSeek API Key" "Meta API Key" "Z.ai API Key" "Command Code API Key"; do`, matching the four provider enums (DeepSeekKeychain.swift:6, MetaKeychain.swift:6, ZaiKeychain.swift:6, CommandCodeKeychain.swift:8). No `MCP <server> <field>` account is copied. RESULT: after a mirror, Dev holds the release app's full MCP server configuration with every secret field missing. scripts/quick_run.sh:10-11 verbatim: 'keeps its own data across relaunches: pair names, MCP sign-ins and the threads made in Dev live only there, and a mirror of the release app would wipe them.' The mirror does wipe Dev's MCP sign-ins (via rsync --delete of the library and by not re-adding any MCP Keychain item) but does not replace them with the release app's, which is the half quick_run.sh's header does not say.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT for the port's secret layout: MCP secrets and provider API keys share ONE secret container keyed by the app's display name, distinguished only by account string; the MCP account format is the literal `"MCP " + server + " " + field` with single spaces. API keys use `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked` (APIKeychain.swift:37). The port's Windows equivalent (SecretStore over DPAPI) must keep the same partitioning and the same four API-key account names verbatim. UPSTREAM DEFECT to record: any dev-mirror tool the port writes must either copy MCP secrets too or say plainly that it does not.

resolutions.finding: G10: R059's footer inventory gives the wrong hosts; the Droppy-column links are absolute, and 'a port copying that footer as written would ship five 404s on getdroppycode.app'.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT on the hosts, WRONG on the consequence. website/index.html:751-760 is the `Droppy` column and every entry is absolute to https://getdroppy.app with target=_blank rel=noopener: :753 https://getdroppy.app ('Droppy for Mac'), :754 https://getdroppy.app/ios ('Droppy for iPhone'), :755 https://getdroppy.app/droplets.html ('Droplets'), :756 https://getdroppy.app/blog/ ('Blog'), :757 https://getdroppy.app/docs.html ('Docs'), :758 https://getdroppy.app/privacy-policy.html ('Privacy policy'), :759 https://getdroppy.app/terms-of-service.html ('Terms of service'). index.html:774 https://getdroppy.app/trench.html ('The Trench') and :775 https://getdroppy.app ('getdroppy.app') sit in the `Connect` column with :772 https://discord.gg/2yAjDnVxgF ('Discord') and :773 mailto:hi@getdroppy.app. changelog.html:147-156 and :166-172 repeat the same absolute set. THE CRITIC'S CONSEQUENCE IS INVERTED: because they are absolute to a different, live host, copying them verbatim produces working off-site links, not 404s on getdroppycode.app. The 404 risk exists only if a port rewrites them as site-relative, which is precisely the mistake R059's inventory would lead someone into. Also note: 7 links, not five, are getdroppy.app sub-paths (ios, droplets.html, blog/, docs.html, privacy-policy.html, terms-of-service.html, trench.html). The Open source column (index.html:761-769) is 6 absolute gitlab.com links including :766 .../blob/main/LICENSE labelled 'AGPL-3.0 License', :767 THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and :768 TRADEMARK.md.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT: the Droppy Code site does not host privacy, terms, blog, docs, Droplets, iOS or The Trench; it links out to getdroppy.app for all seven. A Windows port that keeps a marketing site must decide who owns those pages. Copying the hrefs verbatim is safe technically but points users at Droppy's site, which the port's own trademark rules (never present the app as Droppy Code, never use Droppy names or icons) make an ENGINEERING DECISION, not a mechanical copy.

resolutions.finding: G11: nobody records that build_changelog.py silently drops ## [Unreleased]; and parse_notes appends bullets verbatim into `summary` after an unrecognised ### heading.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT on both. (a) scripts/build_changelog.py:20 `RELEASE_RE = re.compile(r"^## \[(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\](?: - (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}))?\s*$")` requires a digit-dotted version inside the brackets, so `## [Unreleased]` never matches. `split_releases` (:58-72) initialises `current = None` and at :68-69 appends a line only `if current is not None`, so every line before the first version heading, including the whole Unreleased block, is discarded with no warning and no error path. Verified against the data: CHANGELOG.md has 17 `## [` headings (`## [Unreleased]` at :7 plus 16 versioned ones from 1.6.0 at :14 down to 1.0.0 at :352) and website/changelog.json holds exactly 16 releases. At this commit `## [Unreleased]` (CHANGELOG.md:7-12) carries a `### Bug fixes` heading and 3 bullets, all silently dropped. publish_release.sh skips it by a different mechanism: :21 runs `build_changelog.py --section "$VERSION"`, which goes through `extract_section` (:114-131) matching `rel["version"] == version`, and Unreleased never becomes a rel. CHANGELOG.md:5 documents the intent ('Work that has merged but not shipped sits under `## [Unreleased]`, which both scripts skip'). (b) `parse_notes` (:75-111): at :87 `current = HEADING_MAP.get(key)` with HEADING_MAP = {'new features': 'New features', 'bug fixes': 'Bug fixes', 'refinements': 'Refinements'} (:23-27) and a special case for 'thanks' at :84-86. For any other `### ` heading, `current` becomes None, and thereafter :93-95 `if current is None: if line.strip(): summary_lines.append(line.strip())` appends every non-blank line, bullet dash included, into summary_lines, which :105 joins with single spaces into `summary`. So an unrecognised section's bullets land in the release summary with their leading '- ' intact. ADDITIONAL: lines :90-91 `elif current is None: current = None` are a no-op with no effect on any input.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT for a Windows changelog generator aiming at parity: the release regex is exactly `^## \[(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\](?: - (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}))?\s*$`; only three section headings map (case-insensitive after strip+lower), plus 'thanks' into a separate `thanks` array; SECTION_ORDER is ['New features', 'Bug fixes', 'Refinements'] and empty sections are dropped (:106-110); bullets are matched by `^\s*-\s+(.*)$` (:97) and passed through `strip_emphasis` (:54-55), which removes '**', '__', '*' and '_' by plain string replacement in that order; the output JSON keys per release are exactly version, date, platform (always the literal 'mac'), summary, sections (list of {title, items}), thanks; the top level is {generated_at: UTC isoformat, releases: [...]} written with indent=2 and ensure_ascii=False plus a trailing newline (:169-173); releases sort by `tuple(int(n) for n in re.findall(r"\d+", version))` reversed (:134-136, :155). Date resolution order: the heading's date, else `git log -1 --format=%cs v<version>`, else `git log -1 --format=%cs -- CHANGELOG.md`, else today (:42-51). The `--section <version>` mode promotes `### ` headings to `## ` (:126-129) and that promoted text is what the app's About page renders as its cards. Both Unreleased-dropping and the summary-pollution edge are UPSTREAM DEFECTS to reproduce, not fix.

resolutions.finding: G12 / CC7: R002 never states that no .entitlements file exists and that the release chain passes no entitlements; the macOS app ships unsandboxed with the default hardened-runtime set.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. `find . -name '*.entitlements' -not -path './.git/*'` returns nothing. `grep -rn "SANDBOX|ENTITLEMENTS" DroppyCode.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj project.yml` returns nothing (exit 1): no CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS, no ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX in either generator. No checked-in Info.plist: project.yml:43 `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES` with exactly three INFOPLIST_KEY_* values at :44-46 (CFBundleDisplayName, LSApplicationCategoryType public.app-category.developer-tools, NSHumanReadableCopyright), mirrored in pbxproj Release :292-295 and Debug :316-319. ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME = YES in both configs (project.yml:48; pbxproj:291 Release, :315 Debug). scripts/release.sh:60-75 writes an ExportOptions.plist with exactly four keys: method 'developer-id', teamID '$TEAM_ID' (NARHG44L48, release.sh:12 and project.yml:19), signingStyle 'manual', signingCertificate 'Developer ID Application'. release.sh:105-106: `IDENTITY=$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning | sed -nE ...)` then `codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --timestamp "$DMG"`; no `--entitlements` anywhere in the file. The signature is verified at :86-95 with `codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2`, then greps for 'Authority=Developer ID Application', 'flags=.*runtime' and 'Timestamp=', and `lipo -archs` must equal exactly 'arm64'. docs/audit-2026-09-15.md:87 records the posture as accepted: '| P4 | The updater verifies the Developer ID team, the bundle identifier, the version and Gatekeeper before installing: good. The hardened runtime is on. No sandbox, which the CLIs need. | `App/AppUpdater.swift:237` | OK |'.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT that explains the app's whole capability model: it runs with no App Sandbox and the empty default hardened-runtime entitlement set, which is what lets it spawn arbitrary agent CLIs and read the user's home directory. The Windows port has no sandbox to disable, but it must NOT introduce one (AppContainer, MSIX containerization, or a restricted-token child process model) if it wants parity: the agent CLIs need full user-level file and process access. It also means the port has no entitlement declaration to translate; the gate is the OS user's own privileges, plus SmartScreen on an unsigned installer.

The critic is also right that AppDelegate.swift:12 is the single dispatch site for `run`, though `prepare()` has a second, earlier call site at DroppyCodeApp.swift:14 inside `init()`, before LegacyMigration.run() (:15), HangWatchdog.start() (:17) and SwitchLatency.start() (:18); the comment at :13 says 'Before anything reads settings or the library.'

resolutions.finding: CC1: shipped-in-release, unstated by anyone - the capture subsystem links into every shipped binary and its flags are live in the signed app.
resolutions.truth: Fully established under G1. Exact sizes: WebsiteCaptures.swift 1122 lines, TourCaptures.swift 313, TourCaptures+Hydra.swift 305, CaptureRun.swift 41. One addition: the critic's line references 'DroppyCodeApp.swift:14' and 'AppDelegate.swift:12-13' are right, but AppDelegate.swift:14 `return` is the load-bearing line - it is what makes a capture launch skip the entire normal startup.

resolutions.finding: CC2: the capture-run isolation contract exists in the shipped app and nothing in this family states it.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT on every site the critic names, but the list is INCOMPLETE. `grep -rn "CaptureRun\." DroppyCode/ --include=*.swift | grep -v "App/Captures/"` returns 15 sites, and a separate grep for `WebsiteCaptures.` outside App/Captures returns 21 more. The complete gating inventory: (A) storage redirect - Storage.swift:20 `if let captures = CaptureRun.storageRoot { return captures }`, where storageRoot is `<outdir>/storage` (CaptureRun.swift:30-32). (B) defaults suite - CaptureRun.swift:35-40, suite name literal `iordv.droppycode.website-captures`, used by Library.swift:200, ProviderRegistry.swift:161 and :698, TokenLedger.swift:87, WindowChrome.swift:288 and :367, AppSettings.swift:183, :696 and :856, and Wallpaper.swift:75 (the last four via the `WebsiteCaptures.defaults` alias). THE CRITIC MISSED Library.swift:200, ProviderRegistry.swift:698, WindowChrome.swift:288, WindowChrome.swift:367, AppSettings.swift:183/:696/:856 and Wallpaper.swift:75. (C) credentials - APIKeychain.swift:14 `guard !CaptureRun.isEnabled else { return "" }`; MCPKeychain.swift:12 `guard !CaptureRun.isEnabled else { return nil }`. (D) provider registry short-circuits - ProviderRegistry.swift:162, :176, :210, :538, :669, :703 (the critic named only :538, :669, :703). (E) updater - UpdateChecker.swift:133 `guard backgroundTask == nil, !WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled, !AppInfo.isDevelopment else { return }`. NOTE: the critic cites 'UpdateChecker.swift:69' for the API URL; the actual line is UpdateChecker.swift:70, `private static let apiURL = URL(string: "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/\(projectID)/releases?per_page=20")!` with projectID = "86415974" at :67. (F) model and view suppression via WebsiteCaptures.isEnabled - AppModel.swift:276, :1159, :1241, :1249; ChatView.swift:412-415 and :1266; HydraButton.swift:96; EffortSlider.swift:128-129 and :135; DiffInspector.swift:557 and :563.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT: if the Windows port keeps the capture flags, it must reproduce the whole contract, not a subset. A capture run reads and writes its own store under `<outdir>/storage`, its own settings namespace named `iordv.droppycode.website-captures` (wiped at every run), returns empty/nil for every credential lookup, refuses provider probes and background update checks, and additionally turns ON frame-reporting hooks in the chat, the Hydra button, the effort slider and the diff inspector that are off in a normal run. Any subset leaks the developer's real data into published marketing captures.

resolutions.finding: CC3: R002's open question about the three bundled resources is resolvable from SettingsView.swift.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT. project.yml:28-35 adds LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and TRADEMARK.md to the resources build phase with the comment 'The license, the third-party notices and the trademark policy travel with every copy of the app; About shows them under Licenses.' DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:993-1041 `private struct LicensesRow` declares at :996-1000 `private static let files: [(title: String, resource: String)] = [ ("Droppy Code", "LICENSE"), ("Third-party notices", "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES"), ("Trademarks", "TRADEMARK"), ]` and at :1032-1036 loads them once into a static dictionary with `Bundle.main.url(forResource: file.resource, withExtension: file.resource == "LICENSE" ? nil : "md")`, falling back to the literal `The \(file.resource) file is missing from this copy of the app.` (:1034 and again at :1039). The surrounding row is :1003 `ChromeRow(title: "Licenses", detail: "AGPL-3.0 with attribution terms, and the notices for what the app builds on.")` with a `Button("Show")` (:1004) in `.buttonStyle(.glass)` at `.controlSize(.small)`, opening a `.popover(isPresented:arrowEdge: .bottom)` (:1007) whose content is a ScrollView of the three sections, each a 13 pt semibold title over a MarkdownView at `markdownPointSize` 12 in `Chrome.secondaryText` with text selection enabled, VStack spacing 18 outer / 8 inner, padding 18, frame width 480 height 440 (:1024), `.presentedChrome()`.
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT: this is the exact spec for the Windows About > Licenses page that LICENSE section 7(a) requires. Three entries in this order with these exact labels - 'Droppy Code', 'Third-party notices', 'Trademarks' - and the extension-less LICENSE special case (LICENSE has no suffix; the other two are .md and are rendered as Markdown). The port must ship all three files inside the application and render them from the installed copy, not fetch them.

resolutions.finding: CC4: the release-artifact naming chain is one literal reused in five places and no report draws it end to end.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, chain verified link by link. (1) project.yml:13 `MARKETING_VERSION: "1.6.0"`. (2) scripts/release.sh:19 `VERSION=$(sed -nE 's/^[[:space:]]*MARKETING_VERSION:[[:space:]]*"([^"]+)".*/\1/p' project.yml | head -1)` and :20 `DMG="$BUILD/Droppy-Code-$VERSION.dmg"` with BUILD=$ROOT/build.noindex (:16). (3) scripts/publish_release.sh:17 reads the same sed expression, :18 `TAG="v$VERSION"`, :19 `DMG="${1:-build.noindex/Droppy-Code-$VERSION.dmg}"`, :24 `ASSET_PATH="/Droppy-Code.dmg"`, :55 `glab release create "$TAG" "$DMG#Droppy Code $VERSION (Apple silicon)" -R "$PROJECT" --name "Droppy Code $VERSION" --notes-file "$NOTES"`, then :61-65 finds the link whose url lower-ends with '.dmg' and PUTs `direct_asset_path=/Droppy-Code.dmg` with `link_type=package`, and :68 verifies with `curl -sIL "https://gitlab.com/$PROJECT/-/releases/permalink/latest/downloads/Droppy-Code.dmg" | grep -i "content-disposition"`. PROJECT is the literal 'droppyformac1/droppy-code' (:15), url-encoded to 'droppyformac1%2Fdroppy-code' (:16). (4) netlify.toml:11-15 redirects /download/latest to `https://gitlab.com/droppyformac1/droppy-code/-/releases/permalink/latest/downloads/Droppy-Code.dmg`, status 302, force true, with the comment at :7-10 explaining that the permalink is why a release changes nothing in the HTML. (5) DroppyCode/App/UpdateChecker.swift:67 `static let projectID = "86415974"`, :68 `projectURL = URL(string: "https://gitlab.com/droppyformac1/droppy-code")!`, :69 `releasesURL = projectURL.appending(path: "-/releases")`, :70 `apiURL = URL(string: "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/\(projectID)/releases?per_page=20")!` (the critic wrote :69). Background cadence: launchDelay 8 s, checkInterval 6*60*60 s (:74-75); defaults keys 'updateChecker_release', 'updateChecker_lastChecked', 'updateChecker_notifiedVersion' (:77-80).
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT: the whole distribution surface hangs on one asset path literal, `/Droppy-Code.dmg`, plus the GitLab numeric project id 86415974. The Windows port needs the same shape - one stable per-release asset path so a 'latest' permalink and the in-app updater both resolve without a code change - and a host whose releases API the updater can poll unauthenticated. Also carry: the updater reads at most 20 releases per page and picks the newest stable release that ships an installable image; the download card's version literal is NOT part of this chain and does not update with it.

resolutions.finding: CC5: Keychain layout - one service for provider keys and MCP secrets, four API-key accounts, kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked, and sync_dev_data.sh mirrors only the four.
resolutions.truth: SOURCE FACT, all verified. Service is `AppInfo.name` in every path: APIKeychain.swift:31 (add), :61 (delete), and in the read query; MCPKeychain.swift:15 and :39. AppInfo.name is CFBundleDisplayName with fallback 'Droppy Code' (Text.swift:4), so the service string is literally 'Droppy Code' for Release and 'Droppy Code Dev' for Debug. Accessibility is set only on add: APIKeychain.swift:35-38 merges `kSecAttrAccessible: kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked` into the attributes after a `SecItemDelete` of the same query (:34). Exactly four provider accounts exist, one per wrapper enum: 'Command Code API Key' (CommandCodeKeychain.swift:8), 'DeepSeek API Key' (DeepSeekKeychain.swift:6), 'Meta API Key' (MetaKeychain.swift:6), 'Z.ai API Key' (ZaiKeychain.swift:6); all four call APIKeychain.key(for:fallback:) / APIKeychain.setKey(_:account:). MCP accounts share the service with the format `"MCP " + server + " " + field` (MCPKeychain.swift:7-9). APIKeychain.swift is 66 lines total. sync_dev_data.sh:49 mirrors exactly those four account names and nothing else, using `security find-generic-password -s "$RELEASE_NAME" -a "$account" -w` (:50) and `security add-generic-password -U -s "$DEV_NAME" -a "$account" -w "$secret" -T "$DEV_APP" -T /usr/bin/security` (:52).
resolutions.port_impact: SOURCE FACT: the port's SecretStore must expose the same flat account namespace under one container named by the app's display name, with the four provider account strings verbatim and the MCP format `MCP <server> <field>`. The 'when unlocked' accessibility has no direct Windows analogue; DPAPI user scope through Electron safeStorage is the closest and should be recorded as the deliberate substitution, an ENGINEERING DECISION.

upstream_defects: scripts/tour_captures.py:36 - `APP = DERIVED / "Build/Products/Debug/Droppy Code.app"` names a bundle the Debug configuration never produces. The same file builds `-configuration Debug` at :101, and the Debug PRODUCT_NAME is "Droppy Code Dev" in project.yml:54 AND in the checked-in project.pbxproj:326. `subprocess.run(["open", "-n", str(APP), ...], check=True)` at :117 therefore raises CalledProcessError on a clean checkout, so `scripts/tour_captures.py` cannot run standalone at dd2b86e. scripts/website_captures.py:34 has the correct path.

scripts/website_captures.py:164 - `wait_for_run(marker, 330)` gives the `--tour-captures` run 330 seconds, while the app's own watchdog is 600 seconds (DroppyCode/App/Captures/TourCaptures.swift:53) and the comment at TourCaptures.swift:51 budgets 'ten minutes'. wait_for_run then `pkill -9`s the run (website_captures.py:150). The default invocation `scripts/website_captures.py` kills a healthy tour capture 270 s before the app would have finished, after which encode_tour() exits with 'No <name>.png from the last tour run; rerun without --encode' (:213). scripts/tour_captures.py:118 uses 630 s and is correct.

scripts/tour_captures.py:109-129 `capture()` has no launch-detection wait. It starts the 630 s deadline immediately after `open -n` (:117-118) and breaks out of the loop the first time `pgrep -f <marker>` returns empty (:119-123), which can be 2 seconds in, before LaunchServices has started the app. scripts/website_captures.py:133-151 `wait_for_run` is the fixed version of the same loop (its docstring at :136-137 names the problem) and tour_captures.py never received the fix.

scripts/build_changelog.py:20 plus :58-72 - the `## [Unreleased]` section and all its bullets are discarded silently.
